lane: tectonic geomorphology - channel steepness and knickpoints (chi / ksn), NOT scarp shape
title: Power-resolved replication of the lane's mandated first test on chi-normalised steepness steps with the brief's four confounds masked, plus a strike-corroborated (>=3 independent drainages) emission field
status: PREREGISTERED - written before any number in this session was computed
why_this_is_a_new_experiment_and_not_a_r: Every prior first test in this lane (H65-1, H66-1, H66-6, H70-1) used the SAME underpowered test design: hide_frac = 0.20, seeds (20, 21), and 10 orientation-matched random transects per withheld component. That design yields n = 262 scoreable components and a 95% CI half-width of ~0.047 for a component std of ~0.39.

The pooled point estimate has been positive and stable across three independent statistics (+0.0326 H65-1, +0.0404 H66-6 masked, +0.0326 H70-1 crest-only ablation), i.e. the effect is consistently ~1.5x smaller than the CI half-width the design can resolve. The lane has therefore been reporting 'no signal' for what is, on its own numbers, an unresolved signal.

This experiment changes only the DESIGN (more withheld segments, more control transects per component), not the statistic, and pre-commits the endpoint before computing. It is a replication with more power, not a new detector.

statistic.name: dksn_signed, block-centred, confound-masked
source_layers: data/external/dem10_chi_100m_i16.tif bands 1..5 (step_max/1000, step_min/1000, ksn_max, log10_area/1000, zmean) - native USGS 3DEP 10 m reduction committed by workflow 'dem10-chi'

formula.step: dksn_signed - blockwise median of dksn_signed over channel cells in 40 km blocks (climate / regional-gradient control)

statistic.mechanism: Kirby & Whipple (2012) doi:10.1016/j.jsg.2012.07.009 - a step in rock-uplift rate across an active normal fault produces a knickpoint and elevated normalised steepness upstream of it. Perron & Royden (2013) doi:10.1002/esp.3302 - the chi transform puts channels of different drainage area on one axis so ksn steps are comparable between drainages. Gailleton et al. (2019) doi:10.5194/esurf-7-831-2019 - reproducible piecewise segmentation of the chi-z profile.

confounds_masked.playa_or_closed_basin_base_level: u8 band 3 (raised_n) >= 50 - cells the priority-flood filler had to raise, i.e. internal-drainage floors where the channel profile is truncated by a depositional base level rather than by rock uplift
confounds_masked.ephemeral_alluvial_channels: channel & (ksn_max < 10 m^0.9) - unincised desert washes with no bedrock profile
confounds_masked.lithology_range_core_proxy: footprint & (zmean - 20-cell median of zmean > 180 m) - intra-range high-relief cores. NOTE: the depth-to-basement band (training_features.tif band 15) used by H66/H68 is NOT PRESENT in this checkout, so the lithology proxy is DEM-only and is reported as a limitation.

e1_gating_first_test.question: Do channels crossing withheld catalogue segments show larger chi-normalised steepness steps than random lines of the same orientation?
e1_gating_first_test.unit: one connected withheld catalogue component per fold cell
e1_gating_first_test.observed: mean of `step` over channel cells inside a 3-px dilation of the component, intersected with the cell's active domain
e1_gating_first_test.control: mean of `step` over channel cells along N_CTRL random transects of the SAME length and the SAME azimuth as the component, started at uniform random points of the cell's active pool, pooled per component
e1_gating_first_test.control_pool_exclusions: 10-px dilation of (truth | visible) - a control transect can never accidentally sit on the answer or on a visible mapped fault
validity_rules: component must have >= 3 finite channel cells in its dilation zone, else recorded as skipped
a transect counts only if >= 60% of its cells are inside the active domain AND it contains >= 3 channel cells
a component is scored only if >= 25 valid control transects were obtained
e1_gating_first_test.gate: PROCEED iff (mean > 0) AND (bootstrap 2.5th percentile > 0). Any other outcome is STOP.
e1_gating_first_test.precommitted: The gate is fixed here and is not re-specified after the numbers exist. A STOP does not forbid emitting a clearly-labelled research GeoTIFF; it forbids claiming promotion.

e1b_non_gating.population: USGS State Geologic Map Compilation fault pixels >= 300 m from every catalogue pixel (off-catalogue), inside the footprint
e1b_non_gating.role: secondary / non-gating. The board scores this population; the catalogue population is the one the lane brief names in its first test.
e1b_non_gating.note: Prior rounds measured a sign flip here (H70-1 E1b +0.0567 vs E1a -0.0347). It is recorded, not used to override the gate.

leakage_canary.rule: Each input feature is scored ALONE (rank AUC) against the withheld truth before it is trusted. max(AUC, 1-AUC) > 0.90 is leakage until proven otherwise.

emission.surface: strike-aligned corridors joining knickpoints corroborated by >= 3 independent drainages within a common strike corridor (the lane brief's corroboration rule)
emission.support_rule: no dot on a mapped catalogue pixel (the organiser's own statement, forum thread 11516, is that a dot near a known trace but far from any new-fault pixel is fully penalised)
emission.grid: 3.0 px non-maximum suppression, value 1.0 on every retained dot (DTI is monotone increasing in a uniform rescaling of a fixed support, so p = 1 is optimal on the chosen support)

submission_policy.rule: This session never promotes. The submit-OK flag on the download is set by the measured gate: OK only if the gating test PROCEEDs, the leakage canary is clean, and the literal uniqueness rule (max |Spearman| <= 0.90 and <= 70% of dots within 3 px of any registry raster) is satisfied. Otherwise the artifact is labelled DO NOT SUBMIT.

amendments.stage: before any E1 number existed in this session (stage 'cache' had run, 'e1' had not)
amendments.change: endpoint split into a pre-specified PRIMARY and SECONDARY statistic
amendments.reason: The originally preregistered statistic, absolute dksn_signed = log1p(ku-kd) - log1p(kd-ku), is not scale free: a cell with a large ksn produces a large value even for a modest relative steepness step, so transects that happen to cross steep channels score high. Kirby & Whipple (2012) and Wobus et al. (2006) read the RELATIVE step, which is exactly the committed reduction's step_max = ln(ku/kd) (stored as step_max/1000). It is also the statistic H65-1, H66-6 and H70-1 measured, so it is the only choice that is comparable to the lane's own literature.
amendments.primary: relative_step = step_max/1000 (scale-free log ratio), block-centred, confound-masked
amendments.decision_rule_unchanged: PROCEED iff (primary mean > 0) AND (primary bootstrap 2.5th percentile > 0)
